claim: TubeArchivist schedules its subscription rescan using a cron-like minute/hour/day-of-week format and cannot run more than once per hour, with docs warning against frequent schedules to avoid YouTube throttling.
quote: the first value is the minute, second is the hour and third is day of the week as a number... the scheduler doesn't support schedules that trigger more than once per hour... Avoid an unnecessary or frequent schedule to reduce likelihood of being blocked or throttled by YouTube.

claim: TubeArchivist's Rescan Subscriptions task scans subscribed channels and playlists for new videos, shorts and streams and adds missing ones to the download queue; the rescan is meant to run once per day.
quote: The Rescan Subscriptions feature will start a background task to look for new videos from the channels and playlists you are subscribed to... The rescan task is meant to be run once per day.

claim: TubeArchivist is a multi-container self-hosted YouTube media server (8.1k GitHub stars) offering subscription rescans plus full-text search over transcripts/comments.
quote: Your self hosted YouTube media server

claim: Pinchflat uses interval-based (not cron) indexing where the next index is scheduled only after the current completes, supports Title Filter Regex, Download Cutoff Date (YYYY-MM-DD), and min/max duration filters, fully indexes a channel only once then looks only for new media, and self-throttles concurrent yt-dlp operations to avoid rate limiting.
quote: the next indexing gets scheduled only after the current one completes... it's only fully indexed once. After that point indexing only looks for new media... Pinchflat is configured to only perform a certain number of operations at the same time.

claim: Pinchflat is a single-container self-hosted yt-dlp media manager (5.0k GitHub stars) where you set rules per channel/playlist and it periodically checks for new content.
ytdl-sub has no built-in poller; scheduling is external via cron, using a CRON_SCHEDULE env var in Docker (e.g. "0 */6 * * *") or a host crontab entry, with Windows Task Scheduler on Windows.
quote: Enable cron support by setting a cron schedule in the CRON_SCHEDULE environment variable... CRON_SCHEDULE: "0 */6 * * *"

claim: ytdl-sub tracks downloaded videos in a per-subscription download archive JSON file and uses date_range plus break_on_existing to stop at already-downloaded media, letting users grab back-catalog by widening the date range then re-enable break_on_existing for fast incremental runs.
quote: decides what files have already been downloaded by entries in the download archive file... break_on_existing... will stop downloading additional metadata/videos if the video exists in your download archive.

claim: ytdl-sub is a CLI tool (2.8k GitHub stars) driven by declarative YAML subscriptions and passes arbitrary args through to yt-dlp's Python API via ytdl_options.
quote: Lightweight tool to automate downloading and metadata generation with yt-dlp

claim: TubeSync (2.7k GitHub stars) syncs channels/playlists with a per-source index frequency configurable from hourly up to 24 hours, supports a TUBESYNC_VIDEO_HEIGHT_CUTOFF for minimum resolution, and retries failures with back-off timers.
quote: Syncs YouTube channels and playlists to a locally hosted media server

claim: TubeSync is a yt-dlp/ffmpeg web UI with a task scheduler where each source has an index frequency (the interval at which TubeSync checks a channel/playlist for new media), recommended kept as long as possible up to 24 hours.
quote: Index frequency is the duration between indexes of the source... TubeSync recommends keeping the index frequency as long as possible, up to 24 hours.

claim: MeTube (13.8k GitHub stars) now supports subscriptions: it can subscribe to channels/playlists, periodically check for new items and auto-queue uploads, with SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 60 min), SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_PLAYLIST_END (default 50 newest entries), and SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_SEEN_IDS (default 50000).
quote: Subscribe to channels and playlists, periodically check for new items, and queue new uploads automatically... SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL: Default minutes between automatic checks for each subscription. Defaults to 60.

claim: MeTube's subscription/auto-download feature was a long-standing request (issue #76 "Monitor subscriptions for auto-download") that was historically unimplemented before recent 2026 releases added it.

Community comparisons frame Pinchflat as a single self-contained container best for downloading channels/playlists, versus TubeArchivist needing three containers but adding full-text/metadata search over transcripts and comments.
quote: pinchflat vs tubearchivist - compare differences and reviews
